dataset.name: Processed Soil Respiration at the TRACE experimental Warming project, Aug 2015 - Sep 2017, Sabana, Luquillo, Puerto Rico
description: This data package contains processed measurements of soil carbon dioxide (CO₂) efflux collected using LI-COR LI-8100 soil respiration chambers at the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) located at the Sabana Field Research Station near Luquillo, Puerto Rico. The TRACE site is a mature, closed-canopy tropical wet forest within the Luquillo Experimental Forest. These data quantify soil surface CO₂ fluxes from both ambient (control) and experimentally warmed plots to evaluate how long-term soil warming affects belowground carbon cycling in tropical ecosystems. The data files include time-series tables of CO₂ flux (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹), soil temperature (°C), and ancillary environmental variables, stored in comma-separated values (CSV) format and viewable with any text editor, spreadsheet, or statistical software (e.g., R, Python, Excel). Associated metadata describe plot identifiers, measurement intervals, and processing steps. These data were generated to address the research question: How does sustained soil warming influence soil respiration and carbon flux dynamics in tropical wet forests?

measurementTechnique: Soil CO₂ efflux was measured using a LI-8100A infrared gas analyzer with an 8150 multiplexer. One automated chamber was installed in each plot on fixed soil collars, with additional collars deployed for spatial surveys. The system cycled through chambers on a timed program, with pre-purge, deadband, sampling (~2 min), and post-purge phases to standardize chamber headspace conditions.

Chambers recorded CO₂ concentration increases in the headspace to calculate soil respiration. Simultaneous soil temperature and volumetric water content were logged, with external probes used when chamber sensors malfunctioned. Flux estimates were produced using both linear and exponential fits, with fit statistics reported for quality screening.

Measurements with high variability (CV ≥ 2%) or signs of chamber leakage were removed. Chambers were regularly inspected to prevent obstruction, and extreme fluxes were validated through equipment swaps, tubing flushes, and review of raw traces. Verified “hot moments” of high respiration were retained rather than excluded as outliers.

Instrument calibrations in 2017 and 2019 caused systematic shifts in water and humidity readings. Water content values from March 2017–July 2019 were used to correct the data in this study via linear regression. Chamber thermocouples frequently failed, so fluxes were recalculated using independent soil temperature probes. The dataset was filtered to remove records with missing values, negative fluxes, CV ≥ 2%, or implausible soil water content (<0% or >100%). Background CO₂ levels >600 ppm were flagged for additional review.

Corrected fluxes were averaged to daily and diurnal means. Treatment effects of warming, soil moisture, soil temperature, and slope were tested with generalized least squares and linear mixed-effects models, accounting for autocorrelation and variance structures. Analyses were repeated with and without upper-slope chambers to confirm robustness.
